description:
FILED s512 (Fable, 2026-10-07) by the static-parsing review (docs/static-parse-limits-review-s512.md, family C).  Probes in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s512/review/static: p04c-sig-feature-direct (the feature enabled by `use feature 'signatures'` on the same line), p04b-sig-vs-proto (enabled by a module's import: `package Sig; use feature (); sub import { feature->import('signatures') }`), perl 5.40.3 vs ./pcl on main 3ea47a41.

  use feature 'signatures'; no warnings; sub f ($) { 42 } my @a = (1, 2); my $r = eval { f(@a) }; print defined $r ? "$r\n" : "died: $@";
  perl: died: Too many arguments for subroutine 'main::f' (got 2; expected 1)       PCL: 42

perl's rule: with the feature in force EVERY parenthesised list after the sub name is a signature (`$`, `$$`, `@`, `%` alone are unnamed parameters); a prototype is spelled ONLY `:prototype(...)`.  PCL's `_signatures_enabled_at` (#455) is right about WHEN the feature is on (p04-sigimport with named parameters is identical to perl, also through the import), so the defect is the CLASSIFIER: `parse_prototype_or_signature` (Pl/Parser.pm) decides by SHAPE (looks like a prototype -> prototype) before asking whether the feature is on.  Fix: when the feature is on at the sub's position, the head is a signature, whatever it looks like; the prototype reading is reserved for `:prototype(...)` and for the feature-off case.  Where this bites real code: a program moved under `use v5.36` keeps its old `sub f ($)` -- perl itself changes its meaning (and dies on a list argument), so the program's author sees it; PCL silently keeps the old meaning.  Guard: the two probes + `sub f ($$)` (two unnamed params; f(1) dies in perl) + the `:prototype($)` spelling under the feature (a prototype, both sides).  Low priority: valid programs rarely carry the shape, but the divergence is silent.

=== DONE (s513f) ===
One predicate Pl::Parser::head_is_signature answers for every classifier (_sub_head, sub_proto_text, glob-alias facts, Parser2 _is_pure_prototype / native signature lowering / head_record, PExpr anon sub, the anon-signature desugar). Where a pragma PPI cannot see turns the feature on -- the pragma's own line, or a module whose import calls feature->import('signatures') (Environment import_effects, read by module_import_effects, carried by ProtoCache) -- ANY head shape is a signature. Guard Pl/t/sig-vs-proto-01.t (10 rows, 1-6 + 8 fail on main). corpus-diff identical over 111 files. NOTE: the brief's `sub f ($$)` / `($;$)` under the feature are SYNTAX ERRORS in perl (`$$` is the pid variable) -- the guard uses `($, $)` / `($, $=)`. Residue: an anon `sub ($)` whose feature comes from a module reachable only through `use lib` is classified before `use lib` applies (stays a prototype; not-supported.md).
subject: SILENT WRONG: under `use feature 'signatures'` a prototype-SHAPED sub head `sub f ($) {...}` is a SIGNATURE in perl (one unnamed positional parameter: f(@two) dies 'Too many arguments'), PCL reads it as a PROTOTYPE (scalar context, 42); same when the feature comes from a module's import
